license: No LICENSE file (README shows an MIT badge but the repo ships no license; GitHub reports none)
status_note: active but low-frequency; the original TubeGuruji-style 'Bolt clone' tutorial codebase that SamTerces/AI-first-Builder forked
core_problem: Prompt-to-React-project generator: Gemini returns a JSON map of Vite/React files, Sandpack renders them in the browser, Convex stores the chat and files, JSZip exports the project.
architecture: Next.js 15 App Router in plain JS. configs/AiModel.jsx creates one GoogleGenerativeAI client (model 'gemini-flash-lite-latest', key from NEXT_PUBLIC_GEMINI_API_KEY) and exports three module-level `model.startChat(...)` singletons: chatSession (text/plain, temperature 1), GenAiCode (responseMimeType 'application/json', temperature 1, maxOutputTokens 8192, seeded with a two-turn few-shot history showing a to-do app in the exact output shape) and enhancePromptSession. app/api/gen-ai-code/route.jsx calls GenAiCode.sendMessageStream(prompt), relays chunks as SSE, then JSON.parse(fullText) at the end and emits {final, done} or {error:'Invalid JSON response'}; there is no schema validation. app/api/enhance-prompt/route.jsx reuses chatSession (not enhancePromptSession) so enhancement turns pollute the shared chat history. data/Prompt.jsx holds CODE_GEN_PROMPT (JSON schema {projectTitle, explanation, files:{path:{code}}, generatedFiles}), which visibly contains a leaked editing artifact ('Here's the reformatted and improved version of your prompt:') and the whole schema twice, plus contradictory image rules ('use Unsplash API', 'Do not use images from unsplash.com', 'use images from the internet'). components/custom/CodeView.jsx composes the prompt client-side (JSON.stringify(messages) + CODE_GEN_PROMPT), merges returned files over Lookup.DEFAULT_FILE and renders with SandpackProvider (template 'react', externalResources cdn.tailwindcss.com, dependencies from Lookup.DEPENDANCY). Convex schema: users {name,email,picture,uid}, workspace {messages: v.any(), fileData: v.optional(v.any())}; convex/workspace.js exposes CreateWorkspace/GetWorkspace/UpdateWorkspace/UpdateFiles with v.any() args.
core_innovation: None beyond the field baseline; the one cheap trick is anchoring the output shape with responseMimeType='application/json' plus a few-shot exemplar turn in the chat history.
strengths: Format anchoring: GenAiCode is started with a canned user/model exchange that demonstrates the exact JSON envelope, plus Gemini's application/json response mime type; this is the lowest-cost structured-output trick and works reasonably on small models.
Server route separates the streaming relay from the final parse, so the UI can show progress while the parse decides success or failure.
203 stars and 111 forks make it the reference implementation of this tutorial family; useful only as a baseline of what 'AI website builder' means to hobbyists.
weaknesses: Module-level chat singletons (chatSession, GenAiCode) are shared across every request and user: conversation history leaks between users and grows unbounded until the context window overflows.
Gemini key is read from NEXT_PUBLIC_GEMINI_API_KEY; the NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix inlines it into the client bundle.
No output validation: JSON.parse only; no check that /App.js exists, that files compile, that imports are installed; failure surfaces as a Sandpack red overlay.
temperature 1 / topP 0.95 for code generation and 'Add as many functional features as possible' guarantee non-reproducible, bloated output.
Prompt is internally contradictory and contains leaked scaffolding text; image guidance leads to hallucinated URLs and broken images.
Generated project package.json is told to include firebase, @google/generative-ai, MUI, react-icons and framer-motion for a static site; exported bundles are heavy by construction.
No license file despite the MIT badge; legally unusable as code without asking the author (not that any code is worth taking).
Persistence is v.any() blobs with no generation lineage, versioning, or telemetry.
patterns_to_steal: FewShotEnvelopeAnchor: prime the model with a minimal exemplar of the exact typed envelope before the real request → creative_direction / beat selection prompts: show one valid SiteDefinition selection object as an exemplar, then parse with Zod (the Zod parse is what this repo is missing).
Stream-then-parse split: relay chunks for UX, but only accept the final parsed object → renderer/assembly boundary: nothing partial ever enters state.
patterns_to_avoid: Shared LLM session singletons across requests → cross-user state leakage and unbounded context; every generation in our pipeline must be a fresh, fully specified call with a recorded predicate snapshot.
Client-composed system prompt with serialised history → prompt injection and cost abuse; keep prompts server-side and let the model only choose ids.
JSON without schema validation → cannot detect truncation, missing files or drift; SiteDefinition must be Zod-parsed and rejected on failure.
Temperature 1 for structured selection → non-reproducible outputs, incompatible with Decision Manifest and telemetry-driven priors.
Model-chosen image URLs of any kind → asset_constraints require owner-provided or licensed photos with provenance; anything else is a broken-image or licensing incident.
Prescribing a heavy dependency list to the generated site → violates the 180 kB JS budget and near-zero-JS Astro target.
reusable_patterns: FewShotEnvelopeAnchor: one exemplar turn demonstrating the exact output envelope, paired with a JSON response mime type.
StreamThenParse: stream tokens for feedback, commit only the fully parsed final object.
ScaffoldMergeDefaults: deterministic default files merged under model output (weak: model can overwrite scaffold).
adoption_strategy: Ignore. This is the canonical tutorial Bolt clone: raw JSON files map, no validation, shared model sessions, client-side prompt assembly, and a prompt that mandates the generic look. Its only transferable idea, few-shot envelope anchoring plus JSON mime type, is a two-line trick we would pair with Zod anyway. Treat its output ('Well Designed UI' Tailwind card grids with hallucinated image URLs) as a negative reference for what the anti-slop gate must reject.
evidence: configs/AiModel.jsx (NEXT_PUBLIC_GEMINI_API_KEY, gemini-flash-lite-latest, module-level chatSession/GenAiCode/enhancePromptSession singletons, CodeGenerationConfig temperature 1 responseMimeType application/json, few-shot to-do exemplar history)
app/api/gen-ai-code/route.jsx (sendMessageStream relay, JSON.parse(fullText) with 'Invalid JSON response' fallback, no schema)
